description: For Muslims, the Jordanian Personal Status Law No. 61 of 1976 applies in the West Bank and the Egyptian Law of Family Rights of 1954 in Gaza. The wider landscape mixes Palestinian, Ottoman and British Mandate law with Israeli military orders.
energy_note: Your marriage is governed by a 1954 Egyptian statute.
source_name: UNFPA/UN Women, Gender Justice & The Law

aspect: Inheritance at half, and often not even that
description: Sharia inheritance rules give a daughter half a son's share. Enforcement is a separate problem: in practice in Gaza women often do not receive even that, and may be pressured or threatened by male relatives not to file a claim at all.
money_note: Value of the share not received.
energy_note: Half by law, and nothing by arrangement.

aspect: Guardianship sits with the father regardless
description: Fathers are the sole legal guardians of children. A mother with custody may still be unable to enrol, treat, or travel with her own child without the father's signature.
energy_note: Custody of a child you cannot sign for.

description: Men may divorce by repudiation without going to court. Women have access only to limited types of divorce, obtainable through a court, on grounds they must prove.
energy_note: He says a sentence. You bring a case.

aspect: It contradicts the Basic Law and nothing follows from that
description: Analysts note these sex-specific rights and duties are not consistent with the equality guarantee in Article 9 of the Amended Basic Law. The contradiction has been identified for two decades without resolution.

aspect: Fragmentation is itself the obstacle to reform
description: Because the law differs between the West Bank and Gaza, and the two administrations are divided, any unified reform requires a political reconciliation that has not happened. Women's rights are hostage to a separate dispute.
energy_note: Reform blocked by an argument that is not about you.

aspect: EXAMPLE - two codes, neither written by Palestinians
description: Family law for Muslims is the Jordanian Personal Status Law No. 61 of 1976 in the West Bank and the Egyptian Law of Family Rights of 1954 in Gaza. A woman's rights in marriage, divorce, custody and inheritance depend on which foreign statute her territory inherited from a previous occupier.
